title: Encoder · MTF-JEPA-MAE-VICReg
purpose: Discover and develop reusable MTF-JEPA-MAE-VICReg architecture components and encoder tools that operations and application projects can configure, train and compose.
boundary: Own the family definition, supported configuration, portable initialization/preprocessing/training/export/resume surfaces and their scoped evidence, with unimplemented coverage stated explicitly. Cuwacunu and other applications own substantial application training and final docking. Keep architecture, configuration, recipe and trained instance separate; checkpoint scores do not restrict a family to one benchmark shape. Follow the shared encoder component instructions and preserve frozen source and research records.
summary: Develop reusable MTF encoder components and tools; preserve the retained MTF-v1 reference and its model-owned evidence. Configurable construction and portable training coverage must be stated explicitly; provider integration remains proposed.

goals.title: Preserve source and engineering behavior
goals.description: Separate retained implementation and baseline engineering checks from research quality claims.

milestones.title: Preserve the MTF reference implementation
milestones.description: The encoder family and its original version identities were retained in the verified component migration.
acceptance: The family guide and source are present in the imported component; migration records verify preservation without model C++/header edits.

milestones.title: Pass retained baseline engineering checks
milestones.description: The migrated CLI and eight existing baseline test executables passed, including small synthetic fixtures. This establishes engineering behavior for that scope, not operation quality.
acceptance: The migration receipt records CLI build/startup and eight passing baseline test executables with explicit engineering-only scope.

goals.title: Expose a versioned operation-facing provider
goals.description: Preserve native shape, preprocessing, masks, checkpoint identity and source provenance.

milestones.title: Define and verify the MTF provider contract
milestones.description: Choose an explicit MTF instance and return source-linked embedding records under a declared SpaceRef and temporal interpretation. Verify native shape, output selection, masks, preprocessing and fitted-artifact identity without changing frozen historical protocols.
acceptance: Resolve exact version/checkpoint, fit provenance or its explicit limits, source hashes, output selector/native layout, pooling and normalization before an admitted operation consumes this provider; preservation and passing retained tests do not establish this provider contract or operation quality.

Use foundations-record-validation and foundations-temporal-integrity. Record actual per-output support and availability, distinguishing a complete-window embedding from a prefix-valid representation; masks must have documented dependency semantics.

Record-level fixtures cover shape, non-finite/missing data, mask behavior, source lineage, preprocessing changes and the temporal claim actually made. Provider replay and operation utility have separate receipts.
Any diagnostic probe uses or-05-readouts-probe-protocol with an explicitly bound scope; no historical protocol or instance is silently replaced by a comparative default.

goals.title: Expose Hx15 capabilities as a reusable toolset
goals.description: Develop reusable MTF-JEPA-MAE-VICReg components with supported configuration and portable fresh initialization, TRAIN preprocessing, training, inference, export, resume and validation surfaces through documented CLI/library APIs. Derive dimensions and parameter counts from actual architecture constraints; distinguish implemented capabilities from gaps. Keep family, configuration, recipe and trained-instance identities separate. Cuwacunu and other applications own substantial training and final docking; common provider interfaces do not imply shared coordinates or application quality.

milestones.title: Define the MTF tool surfaces and usage contracts
milestones.description: Map existing MTF APIs, CLI and adapters plus selected future building blocks into the common usage conventions; retained baseline tests alone do not establish broad toolset coverage. The component-tool mission and shared encoder instructions govern this surface definition; a checkpoint or application-specific benchmark is an evidence instance.
acceptance: Inventory the agreed loading, encoding, export, validation and workflow surfaces, distinguishing implemented interfaces, reusable components and remaining gaps without selecting a new trained instance or resuming research.

Specify versioned CLI/API inputs and outputs, checkpoint/preprocessing and source identities, native output selection, masks, support/availability, compatibility requirements and explicit failure/abstention behavior.

Define bounded examples and completion criteria for common provider records and operation integration, preserving MTF-owned implementation and historical evidence; do not force universal shape or geometry.

Separate family definition, supported geometry/capacity configuration, experimental or training recipe and each trained instance. Inventory portable fresh initialization, TRAIN-only preprocessing fitting, objective/optimizer, training, export and checkpoint/resume APIs or explicit implementation gaps. Derive dimensions/counts and declare actual architectural constraints; a benchmark checkpoint must not impose the only constructible shape.

milestones.title: Expose and verify the agreed MTF building blocks
milestones.description: Deliver the agreed callable MTF surfaces, examples and provider-to-operation integration checks without substituting historical research scores for tool verification. Coverage must demonstrate the agreed reusable component contract and state configuration/training or provider limitations explicitly.
acceptance: Expose the agreed MTF building blocks through documented Linux CLI and reusable library interfaces in the managed container, using common provider contracts while keeping model loading, inference and export implementation with MTF.

Verify selected standalone tools and a bounded provider-to-operation workflow with explicit native shape, preprocessing, masks, lineage and temporal interpretation; exercise malformed input, incompatible consumer and missing-artifact failures or abstentions.

Retain actual engineering receipts and examples with explicit coverage and gaps. Keep checkpoints and restricted data private; research runs, fitting or new utility claims retain separate actual bindings, protocol and permissions.

For the selected trainable family surfaces, verify representative supported alternative geometries, latent widths and capacities through fresh construction, forward execution, a real gradient update, export and checkpoint/resume. Bind preprocessing and recipe identities, retain incompatible-configuration refusals and record missing coverage. These engineering checks establish reusable components, while substantial application training and docking remain application-owned.
